title: Curvature derivation from a lifted differential across a cyclic square-zero extension
statement: Let $q:R'\twoheadrightarrow R$ be a surjection of commutative rings with kernel $(f)$ and $f^2=0$. Regard $(f)$ as an $R$-module by lifts and put $I=\operatorname{Ann}_R(f)$. Let $(A,d,\gamma)$ be a divided-power differential graded $R$-algebra [def-sfb-divided-power-dga] whose underlying graded divided-power algebra is polynomial, with finitely many variables in each degree. There exist a graded divided-power polynomial $R'$-algebra $A'$ with the same generators and a reduction $\rho:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$, identifying $A'\otimes_{R'}R$ with $A$, and an $R'$-linear operator $D:A'_i\to A'_{i-1}$ reducing to $d$, satisfying the signed Leibniz rule and $D(\gamma_n(x))=D(x)\gamma_{n-1}(x)$ for positive even-degree $x$ and $n\geq1$; $D^2=0$ is not required. For every such choice, $B=A/IA$ with the induced differential and divided powers is a divided-power differential graded $R/I$-algebra. Multiplication by $f$ identifies the $R$-module $B$ with $fA'$: explicitly, $\iota:B\xrightarrow{\sim}fA'$ sends the class of $\rho(a')$ to $fa'$. There is a unique $R/I$-linear map $\theta:B_i\to B_{i-2}$ with $D^2(a')=\iota(\theta(\overline{\rho(a')}))$ for every $a'\in A'$. It satisfies $\theta(xy)=\theta(x)y+x\theta(y)$, $\theta d=d\theta$, and $\theta(\gamma_n(x))=\theta(x)\gamma_{n-1}(x)$ for positive even-degree homogeneous $x\in B$ and $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 09PS (lemma-get-derivation), statement and proof, including the lifting and curvature formula; Tag 09PL (lemma-base-change-div) for the quotient divided powers

proof.text: Starting with the degree-zero polynomial $R'$-algebra, use [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] successively in positive degrees, with the specified generators of $A$, and take the union. This gives a graded divided-power polynomial algebra $A'$. The free left-module descriptions at each adjunction give the ordered monomial $R'$-basis, with ordinary degree-zero powers, odd exponents zero or one and even divided-power symbols. Reducing its coefficients gives the same construction over $R$, hence $\rho:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ with kernel $fA'$ and $A'\otimes_{R'}R\cong A$. The multiplication has the same integer binomial coefficients and signs before and after reduction, and the unique divided powers at each adjunction also agree.

source.place: Tag 09PS (lemma-get-derivation), first sentence; the free polynomial construction in Tags 09PH/09PI.

proof.text: For each positive-degree generator $j$, choose a homogeneous lift $v_j\in A'_{\deg j-1}$ of $d(j)$; set $v_j=0$ for the degree-zero generators. The odd-derivation assertion of [lem-sfb-free-graded-pd-odd-derivations] supplies $D$ with these values and both required rules. Since $D(fa')=fD(a')$, it descends to $A$. The descended operator and $d$ agree on generators and satisfy the same rules, so the uniqueness assertion over $R$ makes them equal. The construction never requires $D(v_j)=0$, and therefore does not assert $D^2=0$.

source.place: Tag 09PS (lemma-get-derivation), first paragraph, lifting properties (1),(2) and the one-variable hint.

proof.text: For any such lift, $d(IA)\subset IA$ by $R$-linearity. The divided powers also descend: if $u=\sum_k r_k u_k\in IA$ is of positive even degree with $r_k\in I$, then every summand in the divided-power addition formula for $\gamma_n(u)$, $n>0$, contains a positive power of some $r_k$, by $\gamma_b(r_ku_k)=r_k^b\gamma_b(u_k)$. Thus it lies in $IA$. Applying the same addition formula to $x+u$ proves independence of the representative. All axioms and the differential compatibility in [def-sfb-divided-power-dga] descend along the quotient. Hence $B=A/IA$ is the claimed divided-power DGA, without needing flatness of $R/I$.

source.place: Tag 09PL (lemma-base-change-div), quotient case, written directly using Tag 09PG (definition-divided-powers-graded).

proof.text: The $R$-module map $R\to(f)$ sending $r$ to $f\widetilde r$ is well defined because $f^2=0$; its kernel is exactly $I$ and its image is $(f)$. Thus $R/I\cong(f)$. Apply this coefficientwise in the monomial bases supplied by the free-module descriptions of [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] and step 1: $\iota:B\to fA'$ is a degree-preserving $R$-linear bijection, $\iota(\overline{\rho(a')})=fa'$. For $b\in B$ one also has $a'\iota(b)=\iota(\overline{\rho(a')}b)$ and $D\iota(b)=\iota(db)$, directly from multiplication and $R'$-linearity of $D$. These identities hold for every graded polynomial lift with the same generators.

Reduction gives $\rho D^2=d^2\rho=0$, so $D^2(A')\subset fA'$. Also $D^2(fa')=fD^2(a')=0$, since $f^2=0$. Therefore $D^2$ induces an $R$-linear degree $-2$ map $A\to fA'$. Every $r\in I$ annihilates the latter module, so this map kills $IA$ and factors through $B$. Composing with $\iota^{-1}$ defines the unique $R/I$-linear $\theta$ with the required formula; uniqueness follows because $A'\to B$ is surjective and $\iota$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 09PS (lemma-get-derivation), proof: factorization of the squared operator.

proof.text: For homogeneous $a',b'$ with $\deg a'=i$, expanding the signed Leibniz rule twice gives $D^2(a'b')=D^2(a')b'+a'D^2(b')$: the two terms $D(a')D(b')$ have coefficients $(-1)^{i-1}$ and $(-1)^i$ and cancel. If $i=0$, $D(a')=0$ and the same identity holds. Substitute the defining formula for $D^2$ and use $a'\iota(b)=\iota(\overline{\rho(a')}b)$ from step 4. Injectivity of $\iota$ gives $\theta(xy)=\theta(x)y+x\theta(y)$ on $B$; additivity handles nonhomogeneous elements.

Composition of operators is associative, so $D^2D=DD^2$. For $x=\overline{\rho(a')}$ this equality and step 4 give $\iota(\theta(dx))=D^2(Da')=D(D^2a')=D\iota(\theta x)=\iota(d\theta x)$. Injectivity of $\iota$ yields $\theta d=d\theta$.

Let $x\in B$ be homogeneous of positive even degree and choose a homogeneous lift $a'\in A'$. For $n\geq2$, the divided-power rule and signed Leibniz rule give $D^2\gamma_n(a')=D^2(a')\gamma_{n-1}(a')-(D(a'))^2\gamma_{n-2}(a')$. The last term is zero: $D(a')$ has odd degree and strict graded commutativity in [def-sfb-divided-power-dga] gives its square zero, even in characteristic two. For $n=1$ the same result follows from $\gamma_1(a')=a'$ and $\gamma_0(a')=1$. Substituting the defining formula for $D^2$, the quotient compatibility of divided powers, and step 4, then cancelling $\iota$, gives $\theta(\gamma_n(x))=\theta(x)\gamma_{n-1}(x)$.
